cards.explanation: The answer is "You are lying." Azariah son of Hoshaiah and Johanan son of Kareah, a commander, join the arrogant men and tell Jeremiah, “You are lying!” Jeremiah is the prophet who just handed them the very answer they asked for (Jeremiah 42:2, 3). They say the LORD never sent him to tell them not to go to Egypt (Jeremiah 43:2). Friends, I've heard some excuses, but telling the messenger he made it up is a bold one.

The answer is death. The men say Baruch is trying to hand them over to the Chaldeans so they may put them to death or exile them to Babylon (Jeremiah 43:3). Baruch is the scribe who writes down Jeremiah's words (Jeremiah 36:32). Notice that this is the men's claim. The text never says Baruch wanted any of it.

The answer is False. Johanan son of Kareah and all the commanders of the forces disobeyed the command of the LORD to stay in the land of Judah (Jeremiah 43:4). Staying was the whole instruction. They had promised to obey (Jeremiah 42:6), and then they went the other direction.

The answer is the whole remnant of Judah. Johanan and the commanders took the whole remnant of Judah (Jeremiah 43:5). That's the men, the women, the children and the king's daughters, along with Jeremiah and Baruch (Jeremiah 43:6). It's like one person in the group chat deciding the whole group is going on the trip.

The answer is True. The text says Jeremiah the prophet and Baruch son of Neriah were among those taken (Jeremiah 43:6). That means the man who delivered the LORD's word to stay is now heading to Egypt with the very people who called him a liar. I think that has to be a strange walk.

The answer is Tahpanhes. They entered Egypt and went as far as Tahpanhes (Jeremiah 43:7). The text says why they went: they did not obey the voice of the LORD. Remember that name, friends, because the LORD speaks to Jeremiah right there.

The answer is to bury large stones in the pavement. The LORD tells Jeremiah to pick up some large stones and bury them in the clay of the brick pavement in the sight of the Jews (Jeremiah 43:9). It's a message with no words yet, meant to be seen. I think that gets people asking questions.

The answer is Pharaoh's. Pharaoh is Egypt's king, and the stones go at the entrance to his palace at Tahpanhes (Jeremiah 43:9). That's no hidden corner, friends. Burying stones right at the front door is hard to miss.

The answer is Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon. The LORD of Hosts says, “I will send for My servant Nebuchadnezzar king of Babylon…” (Jeremiah 43:10). Nebuchadnezzar is the king the remnant was told not to fear (Jeremiah 42:11). The stones are about him.

The answer is Nebuchadnezzar's throne. The LORD says, “…I will set his throne over these stones that I have embedded…” (Jeremiah 43:10). A throne is where a king settles in. Those stones Jeremiah buried were marking the very spot.

The answer is False. The LORD says Nebuchadnezzar will come and strike down the land of Egypt (Jeremiah 43:11). So Egypt isn't safe from the king of Babylon. The verse goes on to name death, captivity and the sword for those destined for them (Jeremiah 43:11).

The answer is burn. The LORD says He will kindle a fire in the temples of the gods of Egypt, and Nebuchadnezzar will burn those temples and take their gods as captives (Jeremiah 43:12). Burning is the word, bakers. The next verse says he will burn down the temples of the gods of Egypt too (Jeremiah 43:13).

The answer is True. The LORD says Nebuchadnezzar will wrap himself with the land of Egypt as a shepherd wraps himself in his garment, and depart from there “unscathed.” (Jeremiah 43:12). That's the LORD's word on how the king leaves. He leaves without a scratch.
